how_to_tell_apart: Slovenian stands apart from Croatian and Serbian Latin with kaj (not što/šta), tukaj, jutri, lahko, živjo, nasvidenje and the future or copula forms sem/bom. Standard Slovenian does not use ć or đ, which are routine in Croatian and in Latin-script Serbian. Shared da, je, ne, se and dobro are too common across South Slavic to rely on. Czech and Slovak look even less alike once kaj/hvala/lahko are visible.
